To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the design of a dataflow DSL can be improved by using quotations instead of type based embeddings, and that the resulting design enables optimizations for dataflow programs that would otherwise be infeasible.

the design of embedded parallel data flow languages can be improved by adopting a quotations based approach, that the bag algebra is an appropriate model for distributed collection processing, that comprehensions are an appropriate syntax for expressing dataflow queries in parallel dataflow languages, and that the intermediate representation should be designed to accommodate for holistic dataflow optimizations.
the design of an embedded parallel dataflow ESDL can be improved by adopting quotations and algebraic bag types in union representation.
